requirement:
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.

The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
The reviewed tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`. I found no gaps and no acknowledgments apply.

**Per-file 80% threshold, exact counts, no averaging, no per-function target**
- `mod[tests]/fn[exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions]` asserts these cases:
  - `threshold(79_999, 100_000)` is false even though it displays as 80.0%.
  - `threshold(80_000, 100_000)` is true.
  - `threshold(0, 0)` is false.
  - 4/5 passes.
  - A second file at 0/1 fails despite another file's high percentage.
  - A file at 7/10 fails even though the average of 100% and 70% is 85%.
- `a_function_below_eighty_percent_needs_no_exception_when_its_file_passes` has one function at 1/3 inside a file at 10/12. It passes with no "Accepted exceptions" section, which covers the "no 80% target within each function" clause.

**Union rule, child processes, any positive count**
- `children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union` combines a parent and a child process whose lines are complementary, and gets 5/5. A later all-zero test does not erase that coverage.

**Selection and freshness**
- `stale_missing_legacy_and_invalid_store_cannot_use_older_success` covers these cases:
  - A stale source change.
  - A missing profile.
  - Missing function attribution.
  - A changed build configuration.
  - An invalid store.
  - An older success cannot rescue any of them.
- The active-build-configuration restriction is tested indirectly. The stale test switches to `other-config`, and the exception test switches configs and leaves `code.rs` unmeasured. This is weaker than a dedicated test, but the store-level behavior sits under the cited selection and freshness requirements. It is not a gap for this subject.

**Unmeasured executable file**
- `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` has `code.rs` containing `fn missing() {}` with no recorded lines. The report says `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` rather than a fabricated percentage. This also covers "absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish no obligations".
- `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` shows `code.rs: not measured — accepted exception` and no `code.rs: 0/` percentage.

**No executable obligations**
- `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` uses a file with only `struct S; trait T { fn declaration(); }`. It reports `no executable obligations — pass` and passes without an exception.
- `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` checks the inventory on declarations, macro invocations and derive-only structs. It also shows that a default trait body and a cfg-excluded function are obligations.

**Exceptions**
- `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` shows the file threshold needs a current accepted review. A missing review fails, and a changed citation or changed outline input invalidates the exception.
- `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` shows an accepted file exception passes the threshold without hiding zero execution. It also shows the review determinations `false` and `{"FIXME":…}` are not accepted.
- `function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file` shows an exception on one function does not excuse other functions or the file.

**Parse failure**
- `measured_file_threshold_remains_checked_when_source_parsing_fails` shows a measured file that cannot be parsed still gets a threshold check, reported as `src/nested/driver.rs: below 80%`.

:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} index.summary
Saved execution-coverage checks compute line coverage from the union of
instrumented file-and-line locations in the eligible current results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, including child processes.
Each location counts once in the denominator and is covered when any selected
process has a positive execution count. Percentages use these union counts,
rather than averaging process reports.
When the current set has no usable instrumented lines, or any current result
has unavailable measurements under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`, combined coverage is
reported as unavailable. The check does not publish measured coverage
percentages or threshold results computed from only the remaining readable
results. Otherwise, absent file or function measurements remain subject to
their coverage obligations.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
